step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-Stage CMOS Op-Amp PSRR and Open-Loop AC Testbench
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.27(a) shows the AC simulation test setup used to measure the open-loop gain AOL(f), PSRR+, and power-supply noise feedthrough of the two-stage CMOS op-amp (Fig. 24.8). The netlist contains two identical op-amp instances with large RC feedback networks (100 MΩ, 10 μF) to maintain DC bias while breaking the AC loop.

equation.formula: AOLDC = A1 * A2 = gm_n*(ro2 || ro4) * gm_p*ro7
equation.explanation: Product of the differential first-stage gain and the common-source second-stage gain.
equation.assumptions: Transistors in saturation; small-signal conditions without heavy resistive loading.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Device channel-length modulation lambda=0.1/V gives stage gains around 35-42 dB each, yielding 65-80 dB total.

dominant_pole_3db.description: 3-dB dominant pole corner frequency of the open-loop response

equation.explanation: Miller-multiplied compensation capacitor Cc seen at high-impedance first-stage output node.

sky130_expected.reasoning: High output resistance at node 1 with Miller multiplied 2.4 pF capacitor places dominant pole around 1 to 5 kHz.

equation.explanation: Frequency at which the open-loop magnitude crosses 0 dB (unity gain).
equation.assumptions: Single dominant pole approximation holds up to fun.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Given gm1 ~ 200-300 uA/V and Cc = 2.4 pF, fun settles in the 10-20 MHz range.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the open-loop op-amp

equation.explanation: Difference between op-amp phase lag and -180 degrees at unity-gain frequency.
equation.assumptions: Zero-nulling resistor Rz = 6.5 kOhm moves RHP zero to high frequency or cancels non-dominant pole.

sky130_expected.calculation: Non-dominant pole f2 = gm2/(2*pi*CL) ≈ 0.141m/(2*pi*0.5p) ≈ 45 MHz > fun (15 MHz). Rz = 6.5 kOhm cancels 1/gm2 ≈ 7.1 kOhm zero. Phase lag at fun is ~ -115 deg -> PM ≈ 65 deg.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Design target for Miller compensation with nulling resistor Rz is 60 to 75 degrees.

psrr_positive_dc.description: Positive power supply rejection ratio at DC (PSRR+)

equation.explanation: Ratio of differential open-loop gain to supply-to-output gain.
equation.assumptions: Small AC disturbance injected onto the positive VDD supply rail.

sky130_expected.calculation: At DC, vout/v+ ≈ 1 (0 dB) due to VDD variation coupling directly to output through M7 source/drain symmetry. PSRR+(DC) = AOLDC(dB) - 0 dB ≈ 72 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Since supply gain is ~0 dB at low frequencies, DC PSRR+ equals AOLDC.

vdd_to_output_gain_dc.description: Gain from AC noise on VDD to the amplifier output (vout / v+)

equation.explanation: Transmission of power supply fluctuation to op-amp output node.
equation.assumptions: M3, M4, and M7 symmetric response to VDD variations.

sky130_expected.calculation: As derived on page 790-791, noise on VDD moves gate and source of M7 equally, resulting in vout/v+ ≈ 1.0 (0 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Miller topology without indirect compensation connects VDD feedthrough directly to output, giving approximately unity gain.

equation.explanation: Differential pair tail current Iss charging the compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Input driven by a large differential step, turning off one side of the differential pair.

sky130_expected.calculation: Iss = 20 uA, Cc = 2.4 pF. SR+ = 20 uA / 2.4 pF = 8.33 V/us (8.3 mV/ns).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined strictly by diff-amp tail current Iss = 20 uA charging Cc = 2.4 pF.

equation.explanation: Output stage sink current I_M8 discharging both Cc and load capacitor CL.
equation.assumptions: Output stage pull-down current source conducts constant current I_M8.

sky130_expected.calculation: I_M8 = 10 uA, Cc = 2.4 pF, CL = 1.0 pF. Total C = 3.4 pF. SR- = 10 uA / 3.4 pF = 2.94 V/us ≈ 3.0 mV/ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: M8 constant current source (10 uA) discharges Cc + CL = 3.4 pF.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent power consumption at nominal supply

equation.explanation: Total static current drawn by bias circuitry and op-amp stages multiplied by VDD.
equation.assumptions: Quiescent DC bias state with inputs at common-mode voltage 0.9 V.

sky130_expected.calculation: Each op-amp core draws Iss = 20 uA (diff-pair) + 10 uA (output stage) = 30 uA. Bias circuit draws ~40 uA. For single op-amp with bias: I_total ≈ 70 uA * 1.8 V = 126 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Low power design operating with 10-20 uA branch currents at 1.8V supply.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench measuring open-loop gain AOL, unity-gain frequency fun, phase margin PM, PSRR+, VDD-to-output gain, slew rates, and DC power.
